paper_metadata.title: Efficient State Preparation for Quantum Amplitude Estimation

experiments.description: Real-hardware numerical integration experiment estimating the integral of sin^2(pi x) over [0, y] using maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation with left/right Riemann sums, midpoint rule, and Simpson's rule on IBM Q Ourense.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: n discretization qubits encode 2^n grid points xi; one additional qubit encodes the objective function g(x). For the numerical integration experiment, the operator A is implemented with Hadamard gates on the discretization qubits and controlled Ry rotations on the objective qubit.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate integral_0^y sin^2(pi x) dx via QAE; equivalently estimate E[g(X)] for g(x)=sin^2(pi x) under a uniform discretization over [0,y].

problem_instance.description: One-dimensional numerical integration of sin^2(pi x) over [0, y] for varying y in [0,1].

dataset_specification.description: Analytic test function sin^2(pi x); y varied over [0,1].

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretize [0,y] using 1 or 2 qubits (2 or 4 grid points) and evaluate left/right Riemann sums, midpoint rule, and Simpson's rule.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Run each circuit with 8192 shots; use MLAE to combine measurements for different k; compare against analytic integral; report absolute error and mean absolute error over y.

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise on IBM Q Ourense
error_mitigation_method: CNOT noise amplification with Richardson extrapolation
noise_model.mitigation_details: Readout calibration over all basis states to build a conditional measurement matrix; CNOT error amplified by replacing each CNOT with 3 and 5 CNOTs, then quadratic extrapolation to the zero-noise limit.
noise_model.classical_preprocessing: Discretize the integration interval and precompute rotation angles for the chosen quadrature rule.
noise_model.classical_postprocessing: MLAE aggregation of measurement results; scaling by y for reduced interval length; error analysis against analytic integral.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Choose discretization qubits, quadrature rule, and kmax; compute controlled Ry angles from grid points.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Combine estimates from different k values using MLAE; compute absolute and mean absolute errors; apply readout mitigation and zero-noise extrapolation.

speedup_claims.conditions: for quantum amplitude estimation with M quantum samples versus M classical samples
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the asymptotic error scaling O(1/M) versus O(1/sqrt(M)); practical performance depends on circuit depth and noise.

speedup_claims.conditions: after spin-echo circuit optimization for larger k
speedup_claims.caveats: The reduction is asymptotic/approximate and depends on the circuit structure; for larger problems A dominates the depth.

experiments.description: Simulation experiment pricing a European call option under the Heston stochastic volatility model using amplitude-estimation-style state preparation and a four-ancilla encoding of transition probabilities and payoff.

algorithm.variant: QAE state-preparation for stochastic processes / Heston-model option pricing

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Four state qubits discretize the stochastic process: one qubit for nu1, one for S1, and two for S2. Four ancilla qubits encode f_nu1, f_S1, f_S2, and the payoff g.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate E[max(S_T - K, 0)] for a European call option under the Heston model.

problem_instance.description: Toy Heston-model European call option pricing instance with T=2 time steps and discretized volatility/stock-price paths.

dataset_specification.description: Heston model with parameters K=1, delta_t=1, T=2, nu0=1, S0=1, kappa=1, theta=1, xi=0.5, mu=1, rho=0; discretized states nu1 in {0.8,1.2}, S1 in {0.75,1.25}, S2 in {0,1,2,3}.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Derive discrete transition probabilities from the continuous Heston SDEs; for rho=0 split joint transition into independent f_nu and f_S terms; use interval probabilities from midpoints between grid points.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulate the circuit in Qiskit simulators and evaluate the probability of measuring |1111> in the ancilla register; compare to the marginal distribution and normalized payoff to verify the expected value.

noise_model.classical_preprocessing: Precompute transition probabilities for the discretized Heston process and uniformly controlled rotation angles.
noise_model.classical_postprocessing: Compute the probability of measuring |1111> and compare it to the marginal distribution-based expected payoff.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute conditional probabilities from the Heston model and precompute uniformly controlled Pauli rotation angles.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Evaluate the simulated probability of the all-ones ancilla outcome; verify against the analytically computed marginal distribution.

speedup_claims.conditions: if the state preparation and objective function oracles can be implemented efficiently
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper presents the Heston model as a simulation example to show state preparation; no runtime or sampling-complexity comparison is reported for this instance.

experiments.description: Additional real-hardware numerical integration experiment for the midpoint rule using a two-qubit circuit optimized to only three CNOT gates.

algorithm.variant: MLAE with aggressively optimized two-qubit circuit

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One discretization qubit plus one objective qubit; circuit decomposed classically into a 4x4 unitary and then re-synthesized to minimize CNOT count.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate integral_0^y sin^2(pi x) dx using the midpoint rule.

problem_instance.description: Same numerical integration problem as exp_1, but with the circuit optimized to three CNOT gates total.

dataset_specification.description: Analytic function sin^2(pi x) over [0,y], y in [0,1].

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classically evaluate the 4x4 unitary for the two-qubit circuit and decompose it back into gates.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Run on IBM Q Ourense with 8192 shots and error mitigation via noisy CNOT insertion; report mean absolute error versus kmax.

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise on IBM Q Ourense
error_mitigation_method: CNOT noise amplification with Richardson extrapolation
noise_model.mitigation_details: Same mitigation as exp_1: readout calibration over all basis states; CNOTs replaced by 3 and 5 CNOTs for zero-noise extrapolation.
noise_model.classical_preprocessing: Classically synthesize the optimized two-qubit unitary.
noise_model.classical_postprocessing: MLAE aggregation and error analysis; compare to analytic integral.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classically decompose the optimized unitary into gates before execution.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Apply readout mitigation and zero-noise extrapolation; compute mean absolute error over y and kmax.

speedup_claims.conditions: same MLAE setting as the main numerical integration experiment
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an additional hardware experiment focused on circuit compression; no direct classical runtime comparison is reported.

speedup_claims.conditions: after classically synthesizing the 4x4 unitary and re-decomposing it
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes this approach does not scale to larger numbers of qubits and is reported for comparison only.
